purpose: separate the MambAtt backbone quality question from the cross-domain few-shot penalty by adding a target-domain full-supervised control on FD003
evidence_supported_conclusions: The project previously lacked a target-domain full-supervised control on FD003; this run now provides that missing benchmark.
Under the current reproduced MambAtt recipe, FD003 full supervision reaches 14.11 mean RMSE, which is far below every current FD001_TO_FD003 cross-domain few-shot result.
Therefore the current canonical cross-domain line still leaves substantial headroom relative to what the same backbone can do when it receives full target labels.
This means the remaining gap on FD001_TO_FD003 cannot be attributed only to the source-domain supervised reproduction gap; there is also a large cross-domain/few-shot adaptation gap.
important_caveat: The gap between the FD003 target oracle and FD001_TO_FD003 transfer results is not a pure domain-shift penalty, because it also removes the few-shot label constraint.
The comparison does not prove source-backbone quality is unimportant; it shows the strong single-factor explanation is incomplete.
next_useful_controls: Run the same target-only full-supervised oracle on FD004 to quantify headroom on the multi-condition target.
If needed, add a target-only few-shot-without-source initialization control to isolate how much of the remaining gap comes from transfer initialization versus label scarcity.
